Seq._doc: Where structured logs go to be searched later; the console keeps printing either way. ServerUrl defaults to a Seq on the developer's own machine and is never checked — the sink batches in the background, so no Seq running means no Seq, not a slower or failing boot. Blank it to turn Seq off outright rather than aim it at a host that will refuse every batch. ApiKey is empty because a local Seq ingests anonymously; only a locked-down deployment needs to set it.

_doc:HangfireHosting: Which role this process plays in the Hangfire topology: 'Worker' runs the servers, owns recurring-job scheduling and executes agent runs; 'Api' registers storage + the job client only, so the pod enqueues and serves the dashboard but processes nothing. Both roles run the same assembly — a two-pod deployment sets Api on the public pod and Worker on the processing pod. Worker is the default so a single all-in-one process behaves as it always has.
_doc:App: PublicBaseUrl is the origin this deployment's SPA answers on. Invitation and password-reset links are built from it — the paths are the frontend's own routes, so only the origin is configured. Never derived from the request's Host header: anyone who can set one could mint a link pointing at their own site, and the recipient is about to type a new password into whatever it opens. Required outside Development; the default below is the dev SPA and a production host refuses to start on it rather than minting links nobody can follow.

App._doc: PublicBaseUrl is the origin this deployment's SPA answers on — invitation and password-reset links are built from it. DELIBERATELY carries no value here: appsettings.json is loaded non-optionally, so a shipped default would satisfy PublicBaseUrlSetting's own "is it configured" check on every host and its fail-outside-Development guard could never fire. Development falls back to the dev SPA from code; anything else must set App__PublicBaseUrl.

Webhooks._doc: The PUBLICLY REACHABLE base URL of this API. Provider webhook registration writes it into GitHub/GitLab, so a wrong value registers a hook the provider can never deliver to. DELIBERATELY carries no value here, for the same reason as App above — a shipped default is indistinguishable from a configured one, and the guard exists precisely to catch the host that never set it. Development falls back to loopback from code.

Cors._doc: Origins allowed to call this API cross-origin (when the SPA bypasses the Vite /api proxy). localhost:5180 is added automatically in Development (matches vite.config.ts server.port); production deployments must list their SPA host explicitly.

Sandbox._doc: RequireConfinement makes an agent run REFUSE to start rather than run unconfined when bubblewrap or unprivileged user namespaces are unavailable. Off here because a host that cannot confine (macOS development, a container without userns) would otherwise fail every run; a multi-tenant deployment on a userns-capable pod turns it on. CgroupRoot is a DELEGATED cgroup-v2 subtree the durable launch creates per-run leaves under — blank means no resource cap is applied.

Agents._doc: RunSpoolDirectory holds each run's captured stdout/stderr and pid file; blank uses a path under the system temp dir, which does NOT survive a pod restart, so a deployment that wants re-attach to work across one points this at a volume. PackAllowedHosts adds EXTRA https hosts a skill/agent pack may be cloned from (comma-separated) on top of the built-in github.com and gitlab.com — anything else is refused, which is what keeps pack import from being an SSRF surface.

Artifacts._doc: Root directory for offloaded artifact bytes. Blank uses a path under the system temp dir; point it at a persistent volume in any deployment whose artifacts must outlive the pod.

Shutdown._doc: Graceful-shutdown drain budget in seconds. The orchestrator's grace period MUST be at least this or the process is SIGKILLed before in-flight background work drains (k8s: terminationGracePeriodSeconds). 30 matches k8s's own default.
